frozen_candidate_root_contribution: Consigning/fixing something into a determinate, standing inscription — setting a content down so that it holds as an established, binding record. The residue is "fixed inscribed standing," which surfaces concretely as marks-set-down (writing, recording) and figuratively as an ordinance-set-as-binding (decree/prescription/assigned term), the latter carried by the internal metaphor of inscribing an obligation.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: Consigning/fixing something into a determinate, standing inscription — setting a content down so that it holds as an established, binding record. The residue is "fixed inscribed standing," which surfaces concretely as marks-set-down (writing, recording) and figuratively as an ordinance-set-as-binding (decree/prescription/assigned term), the latter carried by the internal metaphor of inscribing an obligation.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Across all 319 confirmed occurrences the root ك ت ب contributes one thing: fixing a content into a settled, inscribed standing. This shows up in five internally-observable families. (1) Physical/registrational writing: angels/messengers who يَكْتُبُونَ what people plot (10:21; 43:80; 82:11 كَٰتِبِينَ), نَكْتُبُ مَا قَدَّمُوا (36:12), scribes writing a debt-contract فَٱكْتُبُوهُ (2:282, eight verbal/participial tokens), writing on tablets وَكَتَبْنَا لَهُۥ فِى ٱلْأَلْوَاحِ (7:145), forgers who يَكْتُبُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ بِأَيْدِيهِمْ (2:79), copying out ٱكْتَتَبَهَا (25:5, Form VIII). (2) The revealed Scripture: the dominant noun sense الْكِتَٰب — تِلْكَ ءَايَٰتُ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ (10:1 etc.), ذَٰلِكَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ (2:2), the Book given to Moses/Muhammad, أَهْلِ ٱلْكِتَٰبِ. (3) The record/register: كِتَٰبًا يَلْقَىٰهُ مَنشُورًا (17:13), أُوتِىَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِ (17:71), وَوُضِعَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ (18:49), كِتَٰبٍ مُّبِينٍ = the fixed record of all things (10:61; 11:6; 27:75). (4) The decree/prescription: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ/ٱلْقِصَاصُ/ٱلْقِتَالُ (2:183; 2:178; 2:216; 2:246; 4:77; 3:154), كَتَبَ عَلَىٰ نَفْسِهِ ٱلرَّحْمَةَ (6:12,54), كَتَبَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْإِيمَٰنَ (58:22), مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَنَا (9:51), كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَأَغْلِبَنَّ (58:21). (5) The appointed/fixed instrument: an assigned term حَتَّىٰ يَبْلُغَ ٱلْكِتَٰبُ أَجَلَهُۥ (2:235), لِكُلِّ أَجَلٍ كِتَابٌ (13:38), كِتَابٌ مَّعْلُومٌ (15:4); a letter/missive بِّكِتَٰبِى هَٰذَا (27:28), كِتَٰبٌ كَرِيمٌ (27:29); a written emancipation-contract يَبْتَغُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ / فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ (24:33). In every family, once the form and construction are subtracted, the same core remains: something is fixed into a standing inscribed determination.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM residue: passive كُتِبَ = "is fixed-as-standing" upon a patient; Form III كَاتَبَ/كَاتِبُوهُمْ = enter into a mutual fixed (written) agreement; Form VIII ٱكْتَتَبَ = have fixed-down for oneself (copy/dictate-out); active participle كَاتِب/كَٰتِبِينَ = agent who fixes-down. CONSTRUCTION residue: كُتِبَ عَلَىٰ + patient = the binding/obligation vector ("upon"), NOT the root — the root only supplies the "fixed-inscribed" quality that makes the obligation a standing decree; كَتَبَ لِ + recipient = the assignment/allotment vector; فِى ٱلْكِتَٰبِ / فِى كِتَٰبٍ = locative "recorded-in." PARTICIPANT residue: Allah as subject pushes toward decree/scripture; angels/scribes as subject push toward record/writing; Sulayman/Bilqis toward letter. CONTEXT residue: legal contexts (2:282, 24:33) yield contract; eschatological contexts (17:13; 18:49) yield deed-register; revelation contexts yield Scripture. After subtracting all four layers the non-empty invariant is: fixed consignment into a standing inscribed determination.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The passive-decree cluster كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلْقِصَاصُ / ٱلصِّيَامُ / ٱلْقِتَالُ (2:178; 2:183; 2:216; 2:246; 4:77; 3:154 كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِمُ ٱلْقَتْلُ). Here nothing is literally written and the surface meaning is pure obligation, so the "inscription" residue looks absent — this is the hardest case for a single fixing-into-inscription contribution. It reconciles because the obligation vector is supplied by the construction (passive + عَلَىٰ = "binding upon"), while the ROOT is what renders that obligation a fixed, standing decree rather than a passing command; the same idiom is shown internally to be inscriptional when the object is interiorized — كَتَبَ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْإِيمَٰنَ (58:22) uses the identical verb for "inscribed faith in their hearts," confirming that كُتِبَ عَلَىٰ is the inscribe-as-binding metaphor, not a separate homonymous "obligate." A close second is مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ لَنَا (9:51), where the fixed decree of fate is conceived as what God has "written for us."
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: A near-dual reading takes the primitive as "ordain/allot/assign" (decree-first), with writing and the Book as its concrete realizations: الْكِتَٰب = "the ordained/prescribed thing," physical كتابة = fixing an ordinance into marks, the deed-register = the tally of what is allotted. This frame also achieves universal presence over all 319 occurrences. The data cannot decisively arbitrate direction — inscription-first (fixing→decree) versus ordinance-first (allotting→inscription) — because every occurrence sits at their intersection. What both agree on, and what the evidence robustly supports, is the UNITY: a single "fixed/settled determination consigned into a standing form" is present everywhere; only its conceptual center (mark vs. mandate) is underdetermined by the internal evidence.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Distinctive vs nearest roots: قرأ (10:94 يَقْرَءُونَ ٱلْكِتَٰبَ; 17:14 ٱقْرَأْ كِتَٰبَكَ) = oral gathering/recitation of what is fixed — قرأ is the voicing, كتب is the fixing itself; the two co-occur precisely because they are complementary, not synonymous. Vs سطر (17:58 مَسْطُورًا; 68:1) = arranging in lines/rows, which foregrounds linear layout and never carries "decree/ordain"; كتب uniquely spans record AND prescription. Vs قدّر/قضى (destiny-decree) = measuring-out/settling an outcome without the inscribed-standing anchor — 9:51 مَا كَتَبَ ٱللَّهُ pointedly frames destiny as written, not merely measured. Vs فرض (apportion-as-duty) = obligation without the fixed-inscription residue. Falsifiable: the claim fails if any occurrence carried a pure "read aloud" (→قرأ), a pure "measure destiny" with no fixed-standing (→قدّر), or the pre-Quranic concrete "sew/join troops" (katība) sense with no consignment reading. None of the 319 does; every token instantiates fixed inscribed consignment.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 319 occurrences were structurally assessed (every one of the 52 non-noun tokens individually categorized; the 267 nouns clustered into Scripture / record-register / decree-term / letter / contract sub-senses with verse text read across each). A single non-empty root contribution — consigning/fixing a content into a determinate, standing inscription — is demonstrably recoverable in every occurrence after subtracting form (passive كُتِبَ, Form III كاتب, Form VIII اكتتب, participle كاتب), construction (عَلَىٰ = binding-upon; لِ = assign-to; فِى = recorded-in), participants, and context. The residue is distinctive against قرأ, سطر, قدّر, فرض and is falsifiable. Universal presence holds with no resistant occurrence, so the result is PREFERRED rather than UNRESOLVED. Strength is MODERATE, not STRONG, for two honest reasons: (a) in the large decree cluster (كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُم …) the inscription is metaphorical, so its presence is inferential rather than surface-literal — it depends on accepting the internally-attested "inscribe-as-binding" bridge (58:22); and (b) the direction of the core (fixing→decree vs ordaining→inscription) is underdetermined by the internal evidence, since a dual decree-first hypothesis covers the same 319 occurrences. The unity is robust; its conceptual center is not fully resolved. No numeric percentage was used; unity was tested against the single hardest passive-decree tokens, which reconcile, so no occurrence was forced.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial refutation attempted across all 319 confirmed occurrences (all 5 form types: N 267, V 49, ADJ 1 [82:11 kātibīn], V-III 1 [24:33 mukātaba], V-VIII 1 [25:5 iktatabahā]). Coverage via clustering, per the packet's own coverage_note, with targeted deep-analysis of the resistant/figurative cases: 58:22 (kataba fī qulūbihim al-īmān = inscribed disposition), 6:12/6:54 (kataba ʿalā nafsihi al-raḥmah = self-binding decree), 9:51/7:156/9:120-121 (kataba/uktub = decree-credit), 2:235 & 4:103 & 3:145 (kitāb = assigned/fixed term), 2:178-246/4:77/22:4/3:154 (kutiba ʿalaykum = binding ordinance), 2:79 (fraudulent inscription = purported standing record), 2:282 (binding debt document), 24:33 (mukātaba writ). Every occurrence reconciles with core residue 'fixed inscribed standing / set-down-so-it-holds' after subtracting form (II/III/IV-passive/VIII), construction (ahl/ūtū al-kitāb metonymy carried by ahl/ūtū, not ktb), participants, and context; the proposal explicitly licenses both concrete (marks-set-down) and figurative (ordinance-set-as-binding) via the inscribing-an-obligation metaphor. No occurrence found where the residue is absent. Distinctiveness confirmed against nearest inscription roots sṭr (mastūr) and rqm (marqūm), which denote pure line/mark inscription without the binding-standing-obligation dimension; internal evidence at 33:6 (kitāb described as mastūr) and 83:9/20 (kitāb marqūm) contrasts the standing-record sense of ktb from the physical-marking sense of sṭr/rqm. Falsifiable: excludes transient/non-binding acts and the classical katība (squadron/muster) sense, none of which appear in the packet. Caveat: the contribution is elastic (bundles two surface senses), a mild over-breadth risk, but it keeps a discriminating core and therefore remains falsifiable and non-negotiable-unity holds. Verdict SUPPORTED with zero failing occurrences.
